Phil Weiser

Democratic candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, Colorado · Open seat

Colorado Attorney General

Phil Weiser is Colorado's attorney general, an office he first won in 2018. He won the Democratic primary for governor on June 30, 2026, beating U.S. Sen. Michael Bennet. On July 22, 2026, he named Jefferson County Commissioner Lesley Dahlkemper as his running mate for lieutenant governor.

Where Weiser stands

Housing
Has set a goal of building 40,000 new starter homes. Says he would work with local governments to speed up permits and lower permit fees, and would push for wider use of modular housing.
TABOR and state budget
Says he would lead an effort to change TABOR so the state can pay for key investments. Argues the state lacks enough money for major services, especially K-12 education, but would also cut spending that audits flagged as questionable.
Labor Peace Act / unions
Says he would sign a bill removing the second union-security vote required under the Colorado Labor Peace Act, which he calls antiquated. Says he would work with employers and unions to try to reach consensus.
Energy and environment
Says Colorado should lead in protecting natural resources while keeping energy affordable, using targeted rules aimed at the most damaging emission sources, and says he would enforce environmental laws.
Public safety / corrections
His governing blueprint proposes reducing the number of inmates who re-offend, which he says would also lower state costs.
Technology regulation
Said at the Colorado Chamber forum that he is more willing than Gov. Polis to regulate emerging technologies and social media to protect residents.

Background

  • Colorado Attorney General, first elected 2018
  • Democratic nominee for Colorado governor, 2026 (won the June 30, 2026 primary)
  • Former dean, University of Colorado School of Law
  • Former U.S. Department of Justice official during the Obama administration
  • Former law clerk to U.S. Supreme Court Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg
